keywords.def: used to emphasise that you agree completely with something, or that it is completely right or wrong
quick and sudden; stopping and starting, rather than smooth-flowing
as seen without specialist instruments or specialist knowledge
(idiom) experience of starting to love someone as soon as you see them for the first time
overused phrase or comment (cliché) which has the effect of creating negative or unrealistic attitudes

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 这里是BBC英语教学的《6分钟英语》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Beth. As an adult, when I need to tell somebody something, I just open my mouth and speak.
sentences.zh: 我是尼尔。我是贝丝。作为成年人，当我要告诉别人什么事情时，我直接张嘴说话就行了。

sentences.en: Neil, I'm hungry. Ahh, you'd better get something to eat then.
sentences.zh: 尼尔，我饿了。哦，那你们最好去吃点东西。

sentences.en: And when I want something, it's the same – I just ask.
sentences.zh: 当我想要什么东西时也是一样——我直接开口要。

sentences.en: Erm, can you pass me that pen, please Beth?
sentences.zh: 额，能把那支笔递给我吗，贝丝？

sentences.en: There you go!
sentences.zh: 给你！

sentences.en: We've all been one, but how do newborn babies tell Mum and Dad what's going on before they can speak?
sentences.zh: 我们都曾是婴儿，但是在会说话之前，新生儿是如何告诉爸爸妈妈他们的需求的呢？

sentences.en: That's what we'll be investigating in this episode, along with some useful new vocabulary, all of which you can find on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在本期节目中要探讨的内容，同时还有一些实用的新词汇，你都可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到。

sentences.en: Baby communication is a topic child psychotherapist Marie Derome writes about in her new book, What Your Baby Wants You to Know.
sentences.zh: 儿童心理治疗师玛丽·德罗姆在她的新书《你宝宝想让你知道的事》中探讨了婴儿交流这个话题。

sentences.en: So, what do newborn babies want us to know?
sentences.zh: 那么，新生儿究竟想让我们知道什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, here's Marie's answer: I think they want us to know that they need us one hundred percent, because without us, they won't survive.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是玛丽的回答：我认为他们想让我们知道，他们百分之百需要我们，因为没有我们，他们就无法生存。

sentences.en: Without someone caring for them, babies wouldn't survive, so on a basic level every baby is saying, "Take care of me!" Marie says babies need us one hundred percent.
sentences.zh: 如果没有人照顾他们，婴儿就无法生存，所以在最基本的层面上，每个婴儿都在说：“照顾我！”玛丽说婴儿百分之百需要我们。

sentences.en: She uses the phrase one hundred percent to emphasise that what she said is completely true.
sentences.zh: 她使用“百分之百”这个短语来强调她所说的是完全真实的。

sentences.en: And we'll hear more soon, but first I have a question for you, Neil.
sentences.zh: 我们很快会听到更多内容，但首先我有一个问题要问你，尼尔。

sentences.en: Although they look small and helpless, babies are born with some amazing abilities.
sentences.zh: 虽然婴儿看起来又小又无助，但他们天生具有一些惊人的能力。

sentences.en: So, which of the following statements about newborn babies is true: a) babies are born with a full set of teeth, b) babies' eyes change colour, or c) babies have the same number of bones as an adult?
sentences.zh: 那么，关于新生儿的以下陈述中，哪一个是真的：a) 婴儿出生时就长齐了牙齿，b) 婴儿的眼睛会变色，或者 c) 婴儿的骨骼数量和成年人一样？

sentences.en: Ooh, that's an interesting question. I think I know the answer, though.
sentences.zh: 哦，这是一个有趣的问题。不过我想我知道答案。

sentences.en: I'm going to go with b) babies' eyes change colour.
sentences.zh: 我选 b) 婴儿的眼睛会变色。

sentences.en: OK. Well, we'll find out if that's right at the end of the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的。那么，我们将在节目结束时揭晓这个答案是否正确。

sentences.en: Now, if you've spent time with a baby, you've probably noticed how much they move their little arms and legs.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你和婴儿相处过，你大概会注意到他们挥舞小胳膊和小腿的频率有多高。

sentences.en: Here, Marie Derome explains the meaning of these movements to BBC Radio 4 programme, Woman's Hour.
sentences.zh: 在这里，玛丽·德罗姆向BBC广播四台的节目《女性时间》解释了这些动作的含义。

sentences.en: 75% of their movements are intentional, synchronised.
sentences.zh: 他们75%的动作是有意的、同步的。

sentences.en: They're not jerky – you know, to the naked eye they appear very jerky, but they're not.
sentences.zh: 它们并不生硬——你知道的，用肉眼看它们显得非常生硬，但其实并不是。

sentences.en: They're there to bring us in – the parents – you know, they need us… so all those movements are there to say, "Look!
sentences.zh: 它们的目的是把我们——也就是父母——吸引过来，你知道的，他们需要我们……所以所有这些动作都在说：“看！

sentences.en: Come! Look at me. I need you. I want to, you know, to play with you."
sentences.zh: 来吧！看着我。我需要你。你知道的，我想和你一起玩。”

sentences.en: Babies move their arms and legs to create a bond with their parents.
sentences.zh: 婴儿移动胳膊和腿是为了与父母建立亲密关系。

sentences.en: To the naked eye, these movements look jerky – an adjective meaning sudden and quick, not smooth-flowing.
sentences.zh: 在肉眼看来，这些动作显得很生硬——这是一个形容词，意思是突然而快速，不够流畅。

sentences.en: The phrase to the naked eye means in a way that can be seen without special instruments, like a microscope, or is seen in the way an ordinary person would.
sentences.zh: “用肉眼”这个短语的意思是，不用显微镜等特殊仪器，或者以普通人的方式就能看到。

sentences.en: In reality, these jerky movements are intentional, meaning that they are planned and done for a particular purpose – to catch their parents' attention so they will be noticed and cared for.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这些生硬的动作是有意的，意思是它们是经过规划的，有着特定目的——为了吸引父母的注意，以便受到关注和照顾。

sentences.en: Marie's book is aimed at new parents who are learning to understand their baby's body language, but she also has advice for parents who are finding it difficult to bond with their newborn, as she explains here to BBC Radio 4 programme, Woman's Hour.
sentences.zh: 玛丽的书旨在帮助新手父母学习理解婴儿的肢体语言，但她也为那些发现与新生儿难以建立亲密关系的父母提供了一些建议，正如她在这里向BBC广播四台节目《女性时间》所解释的那样。

sentences.en: Parenting is really hard. Falling in love with this little baby is not… you know, this idea of love at first sight – I think it's such an unhelpful cliché.
sentences.zh: 为人父母真的很难。爱上这个小家伙可没那么容易……你知道的，这种一见钟情的想法——我认为这是一个毫无帮助的陈词滥调。

sentences.en: It will take time to love that baby, to get to know that baby… Many new parents dream about falling in love with their baby at first sight.
sentences.zh: 去爱那个宝宝，去了解那个宝宝需要时间……许多新手父母梦想着对他们的宝宝一见钟情。

sentences.en: The idiom love at first sight means being in love with someone as soon as you see them for the first time.
sentences.zh: 习语“一见钟情”的意思是第一眼看到某人就爱上了他们。

sentences.en: But Marie thinks this ideal dream can cause problems.
sentences.zh: 但玛丽认为这种理想化的梦想会引发问题。

sentences.en: She calls it an unhelpful cliche. A cliche is an overused phrase or comment that has been said so much that it's become unoriginal and uninteresting, and in some cases unhelpful – for example by creating unrealistic expectations, or by making parents feel guilty they are not doing enough.
sentences.zh: 她称之为毫无帮助的陈词滥调。陈词滥调是指被过度使用的短语或评论，由于说得太多而变得毫无新意、索然无味，有时甚至毫无帮助——比如制造了不切实际的期望，或者让父母因为做得不够而感到内疚。

sentences.en: Marie says it takes time to get to know a newborn baby and to fall in love.
sentences.zh: 玛丽说，了解一个新生婴儿并爱上他需要时间。

sentences.en: But for most parents, all the misunderstandings, sleepless nights and dirty nappies are worth it for their amazing baby.
sentences.zh: 但对大多数父母来说，为了他们可爱的宝宝，所有的误解、不眠之夜和脏尿布都是值得的。

sentences.en: And speaking of amazing babies, what was the correct answer to your question, Beth?
sentences.zh: 说到可爱的宝宝，你问题的正确答案是什么，贝丝？

sentences.en: Well, the correct statement was that babies' eyes change colour.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正确的陈述是婴儿的眼睛会变色。

sentences.en: I think you got that right, Neil. I did!
sentences.zh: 我想你答对了，尼尔。我确实答对了！

sentences.en: It's an amazing fact, but apparently true.
sentences.zh: 这是一个惊人的事实，但显然是真的。

sentences.en: Yes, indeed. OK. So, let's recap the vocabulary we've learnt in this episode, starting with the phrase one hundred percent, which can be used to emphasise that you completely agree with something, or that you consider something to be completely right or wrong.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。好的。那么，让我们回顾一下我们在本期节目中学到的词汇，首先是“百分之百”这个短语，它可以用来强调你完全同意某事，或者你认为某事完全正确或错误。

sentences.en: If you describe a movement as jerky, you mean it moves suddenly in stops and starts, rather than flowing smoothly.
sentences.zh: 如果你把某个动作描述为 jerky（生硬的），你的意思是它是一顿一顿地突然移动，而不是流畅地进行。

sentences.en: The adjective intentional means planned and purposeful.
sentences.zh: 形容词 intentional（有意的）的意思是经过计划且有目的的。

sentences.en: The phrase to the naked eye means in a way that can be seen without special instruments, or to someone without special knowledge.
sentences.zh: “用肉眼”这个短语的意思是不用特殊仪器就能看到，或者对没有专业知识的人来说可见。

sentences.en: The idiom love at first sight describes the experience of starting to love someone as soon as you see them for the first time.
sentences.zh: 习语“一见钟情”描述的是第一次看到某人就开始爱上他们的经历。

sentences.en: And finally, an unhelpful cliche is an overused phrase or comment – a cliché – which has the effect of creating unhelpful or unrealistic attitudes.
sentences.zh: 最后，一个毫无帮助的陈词滥调是一个被过度使用的短语或评论——也就是陈词滥调——它会产生无益的或不切实际的态度。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but remember you can find many more episodes, plus a quiz and worksheet for this one, on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 我们的6分钟时间又到了，但请记住，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到更多节目，以及本期节目的测验和练习单。

sentences.en: Goodbye for now! Bye!
sentences.zh: 先到这里，再见！再见！
